problem: Given a rectangular pyramid, find the differential $\text{d}V$ for the volume $V$ of the rectangular pyramid if the base is a square with the side of $a=6$ and the height is $h=5.$

feedback.problem: Given a rectangular solid, find the differential $\text{d}V$ for the volume $V$ of the rectangular solid if the lengths of the sides are $a=2,$ $b=5,$ and $c=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The volume of the rectangular solid is $V=abc.$ Let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}V(a,b,c) & =(\frac{∂V}{∂a})\,\text{d}a+(\frac{∂V}{∂b})\,\text{d}b+(\frac{∂V}{∂c})\,\text{d}c \\  & =bc\,\text{d}a+ac\,\text{d}b+ab\,\text{d}c\end{aligned}
$$

For $a=2,$ $b=5,$ and $c=1,$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}V(2,5,1) & =5\cdot 1\,\text{d}a+2\cdot 1\,\text{d}b+5\cdot 2\,\text{d}c \\  & =5\,\text{d}a+2\,\text{d}b+10\,\text{d}c.\end{aligned}
$$
